— THE SCREENPLAY · EPISODE 01

THE FULL STORY

Soap making is a chemical process that transforms fats or oils into soap through a reaction called saponification.

In this project, we explore the materials, apparatus and key stages involved in liquid soap preparation. The website combines practical learning with interactive visual explanations so that the chemistry is easier to understand.

Follow each episode to learn how the reaction works, how soap molecules behave and how soap helps remove oily dirt.

01Core reaction: Saponification
02Learning mode: Virtual lab
03Focus: Chemistry in action

— EPISODE 04

THE MAKING PROCESS

Follow the seven stages shown in your practical notes. Select any stage to read a detailed explanation. Always use the quantities and instructions approved by your instructor.

Step 1 · Measure distilled water
Start with a clean beaker and measure the required amount of distilled water using suitable laboratory glassware. Read the measuring scale at eye level and use the amount written in your approved practical procedure. Distilled water provides the liquid base and helps reduce unwanted impurities. Keep the beaker on a stable, level work surface.

— EPISODE 06 · MOLECULAR VIEW

THE SCIENCE OF SOAP

Soap molecules have two different parts: a hydrophilic head that interacts with water and a hydrophobic tail that interacts with oils and grease.

When soap is mixed with water around oily dirt, the molecules can arrange themselves into structures called micelles. This helps suspend oily material so it can be rinsed away.

— EPISODE 07 · OUR PRACTICAL

OUR FIVE-STEP MAKING PROCESS

Explore the five stages of our liquid soap preparation practical, documented with photographs from our laboratory work. Click any photograph to view it in a larger size.

STEP 01

Measurement

The required liquid/material is measured and transferred into the beaker using laboratory glassware.

STEP 02

Mixing

The ingredients are combined gradually and mixed carefully to obtain an even mixture.

STEP 03

Heating

The mixture is heated on a laboratory hot plate under supervision.

STEP 04

Filtration

The mixture is passed through a filter to separate unwanted undissolved particles.

STEP 05

Final Product

The prepared liquid soap sample is collected and presented as the final product.

— EPISODE 08 · ANALYSIS

ADVANTAGES & SAFETY

✅

Advantages

Connects chemistry theory with practical learning; demonstrates saponification; shows how soap interacts with oily dirt.

⚠️

Limitations

Alkali handling requires precautions; heating needs supervision; soap properties depend on the materials and formulation.

🛡️

Safety First

Follow the college laboratory manual and instructor's instructions. Use appropriate PPE and handle corrosive chemicals carefully.
